To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caloric restriction in mice induces a differential regulation in the Krebs cycle, resulting in a truncation of the cycle, which may be an adaptation to the gluconeogenic needs of the brain.
long-term caloric-restriction in old mice results in a differential regulation of the Krebs cycle.
long-term caloric restricted (CR) mice show increased Krebs cycle activity in the second half of cycle, decreased activity in the first half, and decreased levels of citric acid cycle intermediates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the beneficial effects of CR, which may be used as a model for the prevention and/or treatment of age-associated diseases, such as diabetes and cancer.
the effects of CR on aging and longevity.
the effects of aging and caloric restriction on the Krebs cycle, a major metabolic pathway in liver, as well as on the levels of metabolites in the cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

long-term caloric restricted mice (CR) display a truncated Krebs cycle with decreased activities of the first block of enzymes (CS, ACS, and NAD-dependent ICADH) and increased activities of the second block of enzymes (SDH, MDH, IDH, and OGDH) with no change in fumarase activity.
the Krebs cycle is regulated by caloric restrictions in a manner that is different from that observed in young mice, and this regulation is consistent with the metabolic needs of the organism.
the Krebs cycle is not a simple linear metabolic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
long-term CR is a potent modulator of the Krebs cycle, which may be a major mechanism by which CR exerts its beneficial effects.
CR is an effective means to slow down age related changes and maintain homeostasis in the Krebs cycle.
long-term CR results in a metabolic adaptation that may be the result, in part, of a decrease in Krebs cycle activity and a decrease in levels of Krebs cycle metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Krebs cycle is a highly regulated pathway and that the regulation of the Krebs cycle can be affected by caloric restriction.
CR induces differential regulation of the Krebs cycle enzymes in the liver of old mice.
the Krebs cycle enzymes are regulated in different ways in old animals.
